newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 17.

text.p: These are leading stories in today's afternoon daily Le Monde, dated April 18.
-- CNCIS intelligence watchdog says it is has raised wiretap quota to 1,540 lines from 1,180 in 1996. Authorised wiretappers are Interior and Defence ministries, Customs.

-- Confidential budget memo says 1997 budget deficit is already headed towards 3.8 percent of GDP but could be held to 3.5 percent with new measures. It goes on to predict 4.5 for 1998 or a flat four percent with new measures. Le Monde has been unable to obtain confirmation from the Finance Ministry but claims "very good sources" confirm the figures are accurate.

-- Paris and Bonn deny collusion to keep Italy and Spain out of the first group of single-currency users. Bank of France Monetary Policy Council member Jean Boissonnat outlines plan for Italy to join later in today's issue of the news weekly L'Express.
-- State-owned nuclear materials maker Cogema contests government auditors' assertions of "serious discrepancies" in its accounts.
-- European car price war slashes Peugeot's 1996 net profit by 57 percent to 734 million francs. Analysts had been expecting about 1.2 billion francs.
-- Elf sleaze probe allegedly leads to Samuel Dossou, personal advisor to Gabonese President Omar Bongo.
-- France heads for drought as underground water levels fall below normal. Three quarters of the country has seen no rain for past two months.
-- One-day nationwide postal strike set for last half of May.
